newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian rebels seized another town before deal.
newsitem.headline: Albanian rebels seized another town before deal.

text.p: Albanian rebels seized another important southern town, Permet, before President Sali Berisha struck a deal on Sunday to hold early elections, rebels and residents coming from the area said on Monday.

The rebels and residents said six people were killed in the fighting in Permet on Sunday. There was no immediate independent confirmation of the reports. Permet is on the main highway going southeast from rebel-held Tepelene.
The travellers gave no further details on the fighting. Rebel leaders in the southern town of Gjirokaster also said Permet had fallen and government troops had fled.
Berisha, facing a growing armed revolt in the south, agreed with all political parties on Sunday to hold a new general election in June -- three years ahead of schedule.

Rebels in the south greeted the news coolly, saying they wanted Berisha himself to resign before surrendering thousands of weapons -- including tanks and heavy artillery -- which has been looted from state arsenals.
